Introduction
A cabin fire far from Earth can't wait for mission control
The problem: NASA’s fire experiment data is scattered and hard to find, compare and interpret. And in a real emergency, a fire can spread before anyone on Earth hears the alarm: a signal from Mars takes over 12 minutes one way, so the response has to happen on board.
Who it’s for: mission planners, crews and fire-safety engineers preparing for Moon and Mars missions, and researchers who need NASA’s fire findings in one place.
Our dashboard: three pages, plus light mode
1 · Dashboard: the NASA data
40 NASA fire experiments, scored 1–10 by AI on one question: how much does each affect fire risk on a Moon or Mars spacecraft? Includes filters, charts and an “Ask the assistant” box.
Superintelligence
2 · Fire Simulation: the SI agent
Always on: it forecasts the fire and chooses the action itself from NASA experiment data, without intervention from Earth. Every decision is logged and replayable.
3 · Risk Tracker: live hazard score
Live Fire Hazard Score (0–100) and 60-second forecast for 4 environments: space station 0 g, Moon 1/6 g, Mars 3/8 g, Earth lab 1 g.

Feature 2 · Decisions, log & replay
Every decision is forecast, evidenced and logged
Contained, with evidence
  • Each action cites the NASA experiment behind it.
Agent log, replay & report
Feature 2 · Memory, readiness & guardrails
It learns from each fire, within strict rules
Readiness & memory
  • Readiness 0–100 per environment and material; riskiest: space station + foam (62).
9 guardrails
  • No inert gas until the crew is clear; act only if it cuts damage by 15%; failed actions are logged and replaced.
Feature 3 · Dynamic risk scoring & prediction
Watching every cabin and predicting what's next
Live hazard score
  • Sensors feed a Fire Hazard Score (0–100); advisory at 55, alarm at 75.
Score breakdown
  • Shows what each sensor adds to the score.
60-second forecast
  • Projects each score a minute ahead and shows its own accuracy.
How the score is built
  • 40% oxygen and pressure, 20% airflow, 40% material.
Honest limits: sensor values are simulated, the fire model is illustrative, Moon and Mars scores are extrapolated, and nothing here controls real hardware.
